title.narrative: Bangladesh floods response - CI appeal EA19/2011

description.narrative: This project is part of a worldwide response of Catholic agencies through the Caritas International network to the disastrous flooding in Bangladesh in August-September 2011, caused by severe monsoon rains. Seasonal flooding is normal in Bangladesh, and can actually be beneficial (the floods deposit sediment on the fields which enhances their fertility). But excessive flooding not only causes widespread damage but requires people to evacuate their homes to live in makeshift camps without proper sanitary facilities, and until the floods recede they may be unable to pursue their normal livelihoods. Caritas Bangladesh undertook to extend emergency assistance to Satkhira District, in Khulna Division which was one of the worst-affected areas. The activities include construction of latrines and training on hygiene practices, support for building temporary shelters as needed (labour and/ or materials), food rations, and cash-for-work for 10-15 days to enable one member from up to 2,000 households to earn a wage from working on essential infrastructural repairs (cleaning up damaged houses and latrines, and repairing roads).
